name: n8n AI Knowledge Loader - Google Drive

parameters.content:
## 📚 Knowledge base: indexing and synchronization
Scans the Google Drive folder (Settings → googleDriveFolderId) and automatically detects the file type: Google Docs/Sheets, PDF (including scans — auto-OCR), Excel, images (described via OpenAI Vision), DOCX, PPTX (auto-converted). Unsupported format → email to the admin.

The knowledge base keeps itself in sync: new file → indexed; changed file (by modification date) → old chunks removed and new ones saved; deleted file → detected and cleaned up from Pinecone. 3 ways to trigger a run: automatically when a file is added, on a daily schedule (3:00 AM), or manually.

## 📋 Overview

This workflow is responsible ONLY for loading data from Google Drive into the Pinecone knowledge base. It does not handle email — that's the job of a separate, dedicated workflow (e.g. „AI Inbox Copilot”), which only READS from the same index.

**What it does:**
- Scans the specified Google Drive folder
- Detects each file's format: Google Docs/Sheets, PDF (including scans — auto-OCR), Excel, images (described via OpenAI Vision), DOCX, PPTX
- Detects new, updated, and deleted files — the knowledge base keeps itself in sync
- 3 ways to trigger a run: automatically when a file is added, on a daily schedule, or manually
- Unsupported format → email to the admin stating which file and why

**Required credentials (3):** OpenAI (embeddings + image description), Pinecone, Google Drive. Additionally Gmail — only for sending notifications about unsupported files.

**Setup steps:**
1. Connect the credentials to every node that requires them
2. Create a Pinecone index (dimension 1536, model text-embedding-3-small) and enter its name + host in „Settings”
3. Create a Data Table named `gdrive_indexed_files` with three text columns: `fileId`, `indexedAt`, `modifiedTime` — the workflow uses it to remember which files are already indexed
4. Fill in the remaining fields in „Settings” — see the note next to it. In the „New file in folder” trigger, select the same Drive folder (a trigger can't read it from „Settings”)
5. Manually run „Start document indexing” to load the initial knowledge
6. Activate the workflow

*Once indexed, activate the separate workflow responsible for email — it will use the same Pinecone index.*

## ⚙️ What to set in the „Settings” node

- `adminEmail` — address that notifications about skipped (unsupported) files are sent to

**Pinecone — REQUIRED:**
- `pineconeIndexName` — index name (the same one the email workflow will read from)
- `pineconeIndexHost` — full index host from the Pinecone console (without https://)
- `pineconeNamespace` — namespace (you can leave „default”)

**Google Drive — REQUIRED:**
- `googleDriveFolderId` — ID of the folder containing the documents

**Text splitting:**
- `chunkSize` / `chunkOverlap` — text chunk size when indexing (defaults are fine)

*Fields related to email, classification, and reply confidence have been removed — this workflow only loads data, it doesn't reply to messages.*

parameters.content:
## 🔀 File type detection and content extraction
Every file found goes through a cascade of type checks (mimeType) and is routed to the right path: Google Doc/Sheet → export, PDF → text extraction (or auto-OCR if it's a scan), Excel → row extraction with header detection, image → content description via OpenAI Vision, DOCX/PPTX → automatic conversion to Google format and export. Every path ends the same way: content/title/source ready to be saved.

## 🔄 Change detection: new / updated / deleted
For every file found in Drive: checks the table to see if it's already indexed and whether its modification date matches — if so, it's skipped. After the loop finishes: compares the list of indexed files against the folder's current contents — files no longer in Drive are removed from Pinecone and from the tracking table.

## ⏰ 3 ways to trigger indexing
1) Automatically — when a new file appears in the folder ('New file in folder' below, reacts right away)
2) On a schedule — once a day at 3:00 AM ('Periodic change check'), also detects updates and deletions (see the '🔄 Change detection' note at the top right)
3) Manually — the 'Start document indexing' button below, for a full on-demand re-index
